title: Task notifications and event groups

spans.text: Goal: apply “Task notifications and event groups” to a real program or device. The key principle is: A notification targets one task and is not a general-purpose data queue. In a project, follow this guidance: Prefer a notification for one receiver; use event groups when several event bits are needed.
QUESTION: What will this example do? Predict the result first.
Serial Monitor prints one event when the task receives a notification.

A task notification sends a lightweight signal directly to one task and often uses less RAM than a separate queue for one receiver. `ulTaskNotifyTake` waits for that signal; event groups fit multiple consumers or sets of event bits. Ensure the task handle is valid and decide whether notifications accumulate or clear.

Key line: `void receiverTask(void*) { for (;;) { ulTaskNotifyTake(pdTRUE, portMAX_DELAY); Serial.println("one event"); } }`
What it does: A notification targets one task and is not a general-purpose data queue.
Why it is used: Prefer a notification for one receiver; use event groups when several event bits are needed.
If omitted or changed: Counter, bit-mask, and overwrite modes have different semantics; sender and receiver must agree.
